subject: Emotions
title: Emotional Bids
description: A short lesson to help you apply Emotional Bids.

hook.text: Your partner says 'Look at that bird.' You can engage, ignore, or dismiss. That tiny moment predicts your marriage.

buildup.text: Gottman calls these 'emotional bids'—small requests for attention, affection, or connection made dozens of times daily.

discovery.text: Happy couples 'turn toward' bids 86% of the time. Divorced couples turn toward only 33%. The math is relentless.

twist.text: Bids are rarely dramatic. 'How was your day?' or a sigh or a laugh—tiny signals that say 'connect with me.'

climax.text: Relationships die from ignored bids, not from arguments. The slow withdrawal of attention is more lethal than conflict.

punchline.text: Love is built in moments so small you almost miss them.

quiz.question: How often do happy couples 'turn toward' emotional bids?
